pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Thallium Toxicity (Thallium Poisoning) THE SMOKING GUN: Severe painful peripheral neuropathy preceded by GI distress, followed by delayed acute alopecia and Mees' lines PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium acts as a cellular poison by chemically mimicking potassium due to its nearly identical ionic radius. It disrupts potassium-dependent enzymatic processes, specifically inhibiting the Na+/K+-ATPase pump and interfering with cellular energy production via mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. This results in severe acute gastroenteritis, rapid-onset painful axonal neuropathy with prominent hyperalgesia, autonomic dysfunction, and central nervous system toxicity. The classic delayed sign—rapid anagen effluvium (alopecia) and Mees' lines—occurs 1 to 3 weeks post-exposure due to thallium inhibiting cysteine cross-linking in keratin matrix proteins within hair follicles and nail beds.
